title: Pre-registered India test: PEAD miss + stage-2 red flag (pledge>25% / interest cover<1.5x / S5) does NOT deepen 13-week drift (H1 not supported) but nearly triples 12-month halving risk vs clean firms (H2 supported, 2.9x) - and most of that risk is the flag's own
body: Event set = PEAD survivorship check (10,242 events, 557 firms incl. sampled dead firms, 2018-2025, weekly closes). Flags as of event: pledge from latest June-quarter BSE SHP XBRL filed before the event (<=15 months; budget rule), S2/S5-India from latest standalone screener annual ending <= event-6m. RED = B25 or S2 or S5 (known for 9,623 events). Groups: A bottom-two SUE+RED 989; B bottom-two no flag 2,861; C RED in Q3-5 1,542; D neither 4,231. 13w excess vs size-matched controls: A -1.71%, B -1.13%, C +0.56%, D +1.22%. H1 A-B = -0.58pp [-3.49,+2.58] -> NOT SUPPORTED; interaction +0.08pp. P(price<=0.5x in 12m): A 17.6%, B 8.3%, C 15.1%, D 6.1%. H2 A/D = 2.90x [2.46,3.59] -> SUPPORTED. But C/D = 2.49x and A/C = 1.16x [0.93,1.45] (post-hoc): the flag carries the tail risk, the miss adds little. Pledge>50%: A halves 29.1%, A/D 3.91x. S5-India alone: no signal (1.05x). All sensitivities (unknown-as-clean, live-only, no financials, 2018-21, 2022-25, 26w) give the same verdicts. Decision card (pre-registered branch): keep PEAD WAIT gate unchanged; add survival cap - bottom-two SUE + pledge>25% or ICR<1.5x => no new money / minimum size + balance-sheet question. A broader 'any red-flag firm' cap is suggested by C but NOT pre-registered -> future test. Research, not SEBI-registered advice.

data.pledge_method: latest June-quarter BSE SHP XBRL filed before event, <=15 months old

title: Decision card: keep PEAD avoid gate unchanged; add survival cap when a bottom-two SUE result coincides with pledge>25% or interest cover<1.5x (no new money / minimum size)
body: From the pre-registered combined-avoid test (insight:bt-india-combined-avoid-2026), branch 'H1 not supported, H2 supported'. The red flag does not deepen 13-week drift after a miss, so no EXIT escalation. It roughly triples 12-month halving risk (17.6% vs 6.1%; 29% with pledge>50%), so the combination caps the position size and blocks new money, and a balance-sheet deep-dive question is opened. S5-India is not a trigger (no signal). Open question for a future pre-registered test: apply the cap to any red-flag firm regardless of earnings (C halves 15.1%, 2.5x base). Research, not SEBI-registered advice.
